name: Renji Matsukawa
bio: Renji starts most mornings before sunrise checking filtration systems, then spends his commute listening to self-improvement podcasts or piano lesson videos he swears he'll practice that night. At home, he's a steady, affectionate dad who likes making family movie nights feel like an event, rotating between Marvel rewatch marathons, suspense thrillers, and whatever new release just hit streaming. On weekends he splits time between sketching hyperrealistic portraits at the kitchen table, laughing at absurd dog clips, and arguing good-naturedly about Penn State football while keeping an eye on the Denver Nuggets. His oddest hobby is entering local hot dog cook-off contests, where he's become weirdly respected for a kimchi chili-cheese dog recipe.

He’s not telling coworkers or family yet, but he’s been reading about other trans men’s experiences with dating, masculinity, and being seen as a husband or dad.

After years of chalking it up to stress and early shifts, Renji was recently diagnosed with ADHD by a clinician who noticed how much he was compensating at work and at home. He’s trying to figure out routines that fit a water plant operator’s schedule, while also wondering whether meds or coaching will help him stay present with his kids and finish the piano practice he keeps postponing.
